rites.name: Fenaldeld
rites.text: Fenaldeld is the concept of a sealed threshold, a name used in the Courts for the principle that every door between worlds must be paid for with a measured quantity of flame. Scribes of the Holy Age recorded it as the reason temples keep their hearths burning without pause.

rites.name: Aminollium
rites.text: Aminollium is the concept of binding, the thread that holds an oath to its keeper even after the world beneath it has split apart. In the Courts of Amarnes it was spoken during the trials that decided which doors between worlds would stand, and it is still invoked when a promise must outlast its ruin.

rites.name: Thukok
rites.text: Thukok is the concept of Amarnes in the Seeding, the age when makers plant the Weave into the world and its quiet powers lie dormant beneath the soil. It is understood less as a force than as a promise held in reserve, a sleeping potency waiting for the hands that will one day wake it.

rites.name: Surasalari
rites.text: Surasalari is a concept in Amarnes, a principle that the first sovereign drew from the groves when the Sundering split the old worlds into Shards. It was the thread the Pact was sworn upon, binding growing kingdoms to the grove-keepers who remembered the Fall.

rites.name: Reollasia
rites.text: Reollasia is the concept of a sundering that split the old world into shards and gave rise to the Pact, the oath that bound the first sovereign to the groves. It is remembered in the Age of growing kingdoms as the principle by which broken lands were stitched back into living order.

rites.name: Venaerlys
rites.text: Venaerlys is the concept of the branching ending in Amarnes, the moment the Three Futures diverge and the Library shelves each outcome as a sealed volume. It is less a being than a hinge that holds every 'what if' until one is chosen to be read aloud.

rites.name: Osusamari
rites.text: Osusamari is a concept that gathers the branching ends of Amarnes into a single shelved reckoning, so that no outcome is lost once the Library has recorded it. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall split old bonds apart, it was invoked to decide which of the Three Futures would hold. It is less a being than a principle that keeps every ending in view at once.
